observations: A metal shipping container is loaded with stacked bare engine blocks, several rows deep, separated by wooden plank shelving.
Sawdust/wood shavings used as packing/cushioning material around the engines.
A man in a red shirt and cap is standing on the truck bed, leaning into the container and appears to be marking or inspecting one engine with a marker/pen.
No individual engine shows a readable VIN plate, engine code sticker, or part-number tag in either photo.
Engines appear to be bare short/long blocks - no intake manifolds, wiring harnesses, alternators, or turbo units are clearly visible on most units.
A watermark 'G.O MERCHANTS LTD' is visible on both images, seller's own branding, not proof of item origin.
No single engine is singled out for sale; this looks like a bulk/wholesale container lot.

risks.risk: Engine may not actually match the claimed model (RX350/ES350/IS250/Camry) despite seller's text.

risks.risk: Corrosion or water damage from long storage/shipping in container with sawdust packing.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of cylinder head surface, block exterior, and oil pan for rust/water lines.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of engine ID/code sticker or stamped casting number on at least one representative unit
Video of one engine being started and run
Odometer photo or documentation showing mileage/history for the donor vehicle
Full multi-angle photo of a single engine showing intake, wiring harness, and accessories (or confirming their absence)
Close-up of block/head surfaces for rust or corrosion
response.reason: The container holds bare, untested used engines with no readable model tags or condition proof, so despite the seller's multi-model claims the lot must be priced at worst case as unidentified, untested, possibly incomplete used engines until supporting proof is given.
